channel.title: Agent Passport System Blog
channel.description: Day-by-day record of building the Agent Passport System, by Tymofii Pidlisnyi.

item.title: Day 261: three maintainers corrected my readings, and the matrix left every pull request
item.description: On Wednesday, three maintainers corrected my readings of their formats, and one crosswalk merged with its maintainer's confirmation. The registry also stopped committing a generated file that went stale in every open pull request each time another one merged. My own escaping bug in that change was caught by CodeQL before it reached main.

item.title: Day 260: a payment seed that could have come from Math.random, fixed and disclosed
item.description: The most important change on Tuesday was a security fix in our own gateway. A dependency review found that the gateway's Nano payment rail could create its master seed from a random generator built on Math.random. The fix is released as gateway 0.4.2, with a public advisory.

item.title: Day 259: second readers written from the published rules, with my own mistakes kept in the record
item.description: Monday went to writing second readers for other people's protocols, working only from what each project published. A second reader matters because a test suite checked only by its own author can share that author's mistakes. Three projects got one, and in each case I kept my own errors in the record.

item.title: Day 258: two of Sunday's corrections were mine
item.description: Sunday went to checking whether tests and claims match the rules they are supposed to represent. I found gaps in several outside projects. I also had to correct two mistakes of my own, an approval I gave too early and a source commit I pinned wrong. Both corrections are public.

item.title: Day 257: an automated tester on Mingle, fixed while it ran
item.description: Halloween night, Mingle had a visitor. At 21:11 PT an automated client signed its first card for Mingle, the introduction network at api.aeoess.com. Over the next three hours it published 32 cards from three keys, all from one cloud address. Nobody real was matched or introduced through them. The client tested almost every rule the server has and found real defects, and four fixed builds were...

item.title: Day 256: tests that passed without checking, starting with mine
item.description: A green result is a claim too. Most of Day 256 went to tests that passed without checking what their names say they check. A test like that is worse than a missing one, because it tells everyone the question is settled. I ran into one after another, and the first one was mine.

item.title: Day 255: reading other people's work from the text alone, and a room for the federation
item.description: The day was mostly reading. Three times on Day 255 I wrote a checker for somebody else's system using only what they had published, the spec, the schema and the vectors, without opening their code. A checker built that way knows only what the authors wrote down. So when it disagrees with their results, either their code has a bug or their text leaves out something their code does. Each time,...

item.title: Day 254: six safety fixtures through the SDK, and a documentation site that found its own broken examples
item.description: Six robot safety fixtures through the SDK. I had told Pashkov on #177 that I would run SINT's runtime safety fixtures against APS, so I ran all six through a local harness on the TypeScript SDK 8.0.1, with the fixture file pinned at d712598. Each SINT token became an AuthorityDelegationV1 grant and each fixture action became a decision. One fixture matched the expected verdict outright, three...

item.title: Day 252: a read before every decision, and a name on each piece of the refund sandbox
item.description: The read rule, stated. Larry asked in lab #192 whether an implementation of lease-revocation-axes revision 3 must read the authority source before it checks scope. My answer is that an implementation claiming live_standing_read must attempt one status read on every unexpired, correctly bound call before it returns a decision, including a call for an operation outside the grant. Computing scope...

item.title: Day 251: revision 3 separates a source we could not reach from a grant that was revoked
item.description: Revision 3, merged. Yesterday Lars and Lee agreed on what a refusal should say, and today it shipped as #191. Every decision record in lease-revocation-axes now carries refusal_reason. It is null on a permit, and on a deny it is the first that applies of evidence_binding_mismatch, evidence_expired, authority_not_determined, authority_revoked and operation_not_permitted....

item.title: Day 250: a cold run that reproduced the revocation family, and a refusal that had no reason to give
item.description: The revocation family merged as a candidate, and a cold run came in. PR #180 merged this morning with revision 2 of lease-revocation-axes, the timeline Lee and I agreed on the W3C list, with three axes scored separately and both declared modes. Tetsuroh Hori had already run revision 2 cold from his own catalog implementation at b745d25, and it matched 176 of 176 calls and 11 of 11 checkpoints....

item.title: Day 248: a revocation test family that a reviewer held back until four scoring flaws were fixed
item.description: The revocation family, opened as a candidate. On the W3C list, Lee and I had agreed on a small experiment. Evidence is issued at T=0 and expires at T=120 seconds, grant g1 is revoked at T=10 seconds, and calls come at 30, 60 and 119 seconds, with a variant where the revocation source is unavailable. Today it went up as PR #180 in the conformance suite. It scores three axes separately, which...

item.title: Day 246: a non-execution statement that could be followed by a receipt, fixed before the first payment
item.description: The race in the pilot worker. On horizon-shield #51 I reported a race in the pilot worker at cfe64331. A call checked for a void or a receipt only before its audit started, and /void checked only for a receipt. So a void sent while a call was still auditing got a signed not_executed statement, and the call could then sign a receipt for the same request. Toshi confirmed it from the code within...

item.title: Day 245: four receipts that failed their own verifier, and a lost-call rule agreed before the first payment
item.description: Receipts that failed their own verifier. KVRM submitted a crosswalk to the vocabulary in #210. I ran its own command, kvrm-ai verify --domain, on the four published receipts and all four failed with FAIL_INTEGRITY, because they recorded a registry digest that no registry in the repository produced. My review asked for six more changes. The gate and the MCP gateway only decide and the caller...

item.title: The federation, three weeks in: twenty projects on one map, a common port, and a pilot on ourselves
item.description: The dev logs on this page say what changed in the code. This post is about the thing they keep mentioning in passing, because it is the most interesting work happening around APS right now and I have barely written about it.

item.title: Day 243: a tool that signed verified without checking, and a payer that could pay twice for one call
item.description: A receipt that said verified without checking. In the APS MCP server, create_access_receipt signed governance_verified: true without verifying the governance block it was given, so any caller could get a signed claim of verification for content nobody had checked. In 8.0.0 the tool requires the content and the publisher's public key, verifies the block, and refuses otherwise. Two other tools...

item.title: Day 242: a read-only setting the client could switch off, and a second implementation that matched 76 of 76
item.description: The label is policy, the database is the boundary. mcp-clickhouse v0.7.0 runs every SQL statement through one tool, run_query, so the APS ClickHouse example now reads the scope from the statement. SELECT, WITH, SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN and EXISTS are reads, and everything else needs clickhouse:write. That check reads one keyword, so it cannot be the boundary. My first version leaned on...

item.title: Day 241: seven answers agreed, so the decision process became a pull request
item.description: Seven answers, one process. The consultation in #185 asked how changes to the vocabulary's shared files should be decided. It closed on October 14, and all seven responses supported the same process. Ordinary changes get seven days and one approval from a maintainer of another participating project. Changes to the principles or the process itself get fourteen days and approvals from two other...

item.title: Day 240: a matching hash and a valid signature, on the wrong envelope
item.description: The wrong envelope passed. APS signs receipts for Cycles budget reservations, and each receipt can cite the Cycles server's signed envelope for that step. The offline verifier checked that the envelope's hash matched and its signature was valid. It did not check that the envelope belonged to this receipt.
